name: Kraaft
subcategory: field team messaging and site reports
tagline: Messaging and photo-based site reporting for construction and field crews, organised by job site.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core idea is a group chat per job site where photos, locations and form answers get filed into a structured record you can export as a PDF report. That is a very buildable shape: a web app with per-project channels, image upload, a few custom fields, and a report generator. The gap is everything that makes it work on a muddy site: a real mobile app, camera and GPS capture, offline queueing, and push notifications for people who do not read email. You also have to convince a crew of subcontractors to install your thing, which is the actual product problem. Solo or for one small team you can get there in a weekend; for a fleet of sites with external partners, you will quietly rebuild a messaging platform.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted web app with one channel per job site where anyone can post photos with notes, tag them to a checklist or custom fields, and export the whole site log as a dated PDF report.
requirements: A small server or VPS with Postgres and object storage for photos
A domain and HTTPS so phone cameras and geolocation work in the browser
Each crew member on a shared link or simple magic-link login
Optional: a push service or just rely on SMS or WhatsApp nudges
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps with offline capture that survives a basement with no signal
Push notifications and the habit loop that makes a crew actually post
Polished PDF and Excel report templates that a client or insurer accepts without comment
Easy onboarding for subcontractors who will not create an account for your side project
Support, backups, and someone to blame when the photo evidence for a dispute is missing
moatNotes: The value is multi-party adoption on site, not the data model. Once six months of photo evidence lives there, nobody is migrating mid-project.
whyPeopleStillPay: Field teams pay for Kraaft because the hard part is not storing photos, it is getting a dozen people with dirty gloves and bad signal to consistently log what happened, then turning that into a report a client will accept. That needs native apps, offline sync, push nudges and onboarding that works for someone who joined the site this morning. A self-hosted web app covers a single disciplined team on a single project. It does not cover the social problem of getting subcontractors to use your tool, or the liability problem of being the only copy of the evidence.
notes: Buildable as a site log, not as a thing your subcontractors will actually open.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted web app called SiteLog: a per-job-site photo and message log for a small construction crew, with PDF report export.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js with TypeScript, App Router
- Postgres via Prisma
- Photos stored on local disk under ./uploads, served through an authenticated route
- Tailwind for styling
- Auth: magic-link email via a single SMTP config in .env, plus per-site invite links that create a named guest session
- PDF generation server-side with Playwright printing a styled HTML report page

Data model:
- Site: name, address, client, status, createdAt
- Membership: user or guest name, site, role (owner, member)
- Entry: site, author, body text, timestamp, optional latitude/longitude, optional category enum (progress, issue, delivery, safety), array of Photos
- Photo: entry, filename, width, height, takenAt
- Checklist: site, items with label and done flag and optional linked Entry

Features that are in scope:
- Site list, then a chronological feed per site, newest first
- Mobile-first entry composer: capture or pick multiple photos, type a note, pick a category, optionally attach browser geolocation
- Client-side image resize to max 1600px before upload, strip EXIF except timestamp
- Filter the feed by category, author, and date range
- Per-site checklist where ticking an item can link to the entry that proves it
- Report export: pick a date range, generate a PDF with a cover page (site, client, date range), then entries grouped by day with photos two per row and captions
- CSV export of all entries for a site

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Native mobile apps, push notifications, offline sync
- Real-time websockets, typing indicators, read receipts
- Billing, org hierarchy, telemetry, analytics
- Any third-party cloud storage or SaaS dependency

Requirements:
- All secrets in .env: DATABASE_URL, SMTP_URL, APP_URL, SESSION_SECRET. Ship .env.example.
- Single docker-compose with app plus postgres, one command to start
- Seed script creating two sites with a dozen entries and placeholder images so the PDF export is demoable immediately
- README with setup, how invite links work, and where photos live for backup
- Works as an installable PWA with a manifest and an add-to-home-screen hint on mobile
